newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate falls to 10.892 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate falls to 10.892 pct.

text.p: The benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to an average of 10.892 percent at the regular auction on Tuesday from 11.166 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The auction was postponed from its normal Monday after heavy rains brought financial markets in the Philippine capital to a halt.
For the 91-day bills, the auction committee awarded one billion pesos out of the 5.625 billion in tenders.
The 182-day average rate was 11.348 percent compared to 11.772 percent last week with 5.5 billion pesos awared from total tenders of 13.175 billion.
The 364-day average was 11.809 percent against 12.255 percent last week with two billion pesos awarded from the 19.612 billion in bids.
"It's a sign the market is already becoming more normal," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters of the drop in rates.
He noted that bill rates had fallen despite the central bank increase in its term rates last week.
The Bank was forced to raise interest rates earlier this month to defend the peso following the problems of the Thai baht.
"Therefore considering that scenario, it's a huge drop in the (T-bill) rates," he said.
